I am proud to represent Washington’s 7th district and stand up for working people every single day. As your Congresswoman, I've worked to protect our democracy, raise wages, lower costs, build affordable housing, protect abortion rights, and fight climate change. I’m leading the fight for the Medicare for All Act to ensure that universal healthcare is a right, not a privilege. I also lead landmark legislation to make higher education tuition-free, guarantee housing as a human right, expand workers’ rights, raise the federal minimum wage, implement humane immigration reform, and establish an ultra-millionaire wealth tax. I lead bipartisan bills that ban stock trading for Members of Congress and protect Americans from government spying. I’m doing everything possible to get money out of politics and reform the Supreme Court. I’ve been on the frontlines of holding Trump accountable, including around the lawless ICE and CBP actions that have kidnapped and disappeared our neighbors. I established the Monopoly Busters Caucus to fight consolidation, corporate greed, and price-gouging. I have authored a War Powers Resolution to end Trump’s illegal war in Iran and worked with Epstein survivors to get justice against predators and pedophiles. I’ve held over 130 town halls and helped thousands of constituents, including veterans and seniors, secure over $25 million in federal benefits. My office has brought home more than $70 million in new federal investments for housing, transportation, jobs, and public safety. I’m proud to represent a diverse, innovative and compassionate district. I have never taken corporate PAC money because I fight for working people, not the billionaires and giant corporations. I would be deeply honored to have your vote. Endorsements Labor unions including Washington State Labor Council, WFSE, UFCW 3000, NEA/WEA, and Washington State Building & Construction Trades Council. Planned Parenthood, Sierra Club, and the King County Democrats.

I am running to bring independence, principled judgment, and respect for the rule of law to the Washington Supreme Court. An independent court protects constitutional rights, ensures equal justice, and serves as a final and balanced check within our system of government. The role of the Supreme Court is to apply the constitution and laws as written, not rewrite them. For more than 30 years I have represented clients at all levels of Washington’s court system, including more than a dozen Washington Supreme Court cases. As a tax and constitutional attorney, I work on complex issues that directly affect Washington families and businesses. I have also taught at the University of Washington School of Law for over 20 years. I learned the value of hard work, integrity, and public service early, working at my grandparents’ restaurant and watching my father serve as Alaska’s attorney general. Washington deserves justices who will apply the law predictably, as written, and without favoring any political agenda. My commitment is to protect your constitutional rights and work to make the Washington Supreme Court accountable and worthy of your trust. Take politics out of the courtroom. Vote Scott Edwards, Position 1.

He will protect your individual rights and the judicial independence that is currently under threat. Dave’s innovative criminal justice reforms have been recognized nationwide. He has collaborated with legislative Democrats and Republicans to help our trial courts address crime and addiction with compassion and accountability. However, our Supreme Court’s decisions have weakened that response. As a justice, he will help fix current problems and build towards lasting and effective solutions. Our Supreme Court needs Dave’s unique perspective gained from his significant trial judge experience. That experience, integrity, and steady judgment are exactly what’s needed to restore trust in, and improve, our courts. Vote Judge Dave Larson for Supreme Court.

As King County’s first woman and first person of color to serve as Prosecutor, I have spent the past four years fulfilling my promise to keep our neighborhoods safe, reduce property crime, and protect survivors and the most vulnerable. Keeping that commitment requires proven vision, hands-on leadership and experience – qualities I possess and have strengthened since entering office. Under my leadership, the Prosecutor’s Office prosecutes violent crimes, sexual assaults, and property crimes daily. Since my election, I have expanded support for survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault, invested in alternative sentencing for veterans, youth, and individuals facing behavioral health and addiction challenges, and prioritized juvenile justice reform. My commitment to reducing gun violence shows in a nearly 50% reduction in gun homicides since 2023. I also worked to enact Washington’s strongest Extreme Risk Protection Order policies, a statewide ban on high-capacity magazines and ghost guns, and tools that help law enforcement track weapons used in crime. I am proud of the work accomplished over the past four years: developing fair and effective criminal justice policies and reforms, leading a team of nearly 600 professionals, building trusted partnerships with law enforcement, public defenders, business and community leaders, and advocates for equity and justice. There is still important work to do, and I am ready to continue to ensure that our county is safe for everyone. I am proudly endorsed by former Governors Gary Locke and Christine Gregoire; Executive Girmay Zahilay; former Seattle Mayor Bruce Harrell; the Alliance for Gun Responsibility; labor unions, King County Democrat organizations; dozens of county and city leaders; retired justices; and former U. S. Attorneys.

Thank you for entrusting me to lead the Department of Elections for the past decade. In that time, we have added more than 80 secure ballot drop boxes, in-person voting centers, election materials in four new languages, ballot alerts, and new layers of physical and cybersecurity. We have also implemented national award-winning programs like the Voter Education Fund, our Civic Engagement Internship, and a robust Bipartisan Observer Program. My parents instilled a sense of responsibility in my sister and me to contribute to our community and serve a greater purpose. In fact, it was when my father was running for Mayor of Enumclaw that I saw and applied for a job at the Department of Elections, twenty-six years ago. I fell in love with the work – ensuring every eligible voter could have their voice heard and working to protect one of our most critical institutions. I remain just as passionate and committed today to improving our voting experience and maintaining a steadfast, transparent, and nonpartisan elections department. From Olympia to D. C. , I will continue to advocate to ensure every person has meaningful access to their right to vote. Thank you for voting!

Senior Appraiser, City of Seattle; Former King County Hearing Examiner

The Assessor's office touches every person's ability to stay in their home. Rising property taxes are pushing homeowners, renters, and small businesses out of their communities, and too many people don't trust that the system is treating them fairly. King County needs an accurate, fair, and transparent Assessor's office that works for everyone. I'm a fifth-generation Seattleite and the only candidate in this race who has actually done the valuation work this office depends on. As Senior Appraiser for the City of Seattle, I appraise public properties daily, ensuring real estate decisions serve the public interest. My career has included commercial valuation in the private sector. Serving as a Hearing Examiner on the King County Board of Appeals and Equalization, I've sat across the table from homeowners fighting to stay in their communities while corporate landowners brought teams of experts to secure tax reductions. I understand both sides of this system. I've lived in income-restricted housing. I know what financial pressure looks like from the inside, and it's why I'm a proud PROTEC17 shop steward. I'll bring real relief for homeowners and renters, and transparency and accountability to a system many people don't fully understand. In Olympia, I'll push to establish homestead protections for primary residences to help homeowners manage rising costs, and create a renter's tax credit to give tenants relief from rising housing costs as well. I'm proud to be endorsed by the Seattle Times, the Stranger, King County Executive Girmay Zahilay, Chief Deputy Assessor Al Dams, King County Councilmembers Claudia Balducci, Sarah Perry, and Rhonda Lewis, King County Democrats, eleven legislative district Democratic organizations, Seattle Councilmembers Eddie Lin and Dionne Foster, multiple labor unions, and Danny Hagen, President of the Washington State Association of County Assessors, among others. They trust my professional expertise to lead this department.

background.text: B. A. Criminal Justice, Washington State University
Small Family Business Owner, CAPR King County Chapter President

The King County Assessor is far more than an appraiser—it’s absolutely a leadership role, of one of the largest public offices affecting every property owner. While the office does employ appraisal staff, the Assessor's responsibility ensures the entire system operates transparently, consistently, fairly, and in accordance with the law. I have studied our property tax system from the taxpayers perspective, analyzing assessment data, researching mass appraisal practices, public records requests, appealing assessments, reviewing BoE decisions, and developed comprehensive audit proposals identifying significant areas for reform. That experience gives me something many candidates cannot claim: a taxpayer's perspective on how the system actually functions in practice. My campaign isn’t about making minor adjustments to the status quo. It’s about pursuing meaningful, system-wide reforms that protect taxpayers, strengthen property rights, ensures due process and helps ensure people aren’t taxed out of their homes. Government should be judged by results—not intentions. Our current assessment system is required to produce fair and uniform assessments, but if that system does not produce the results required by law, we have a responsibility to examine it honestly, measure its performance, and improve it. Property owners deserve information they can understand. They deserve parcel-specific breakdowns on their individual property valuations—not simply a final number. They deserve due process, timely appeals and logical evidentiary standards, and should never need to become valuation experts or pay for professional help, simply to challenge their assessment. I’m a King County resident, small business owner, and President of the King County CAPR chapter. I’m not a politician. Government works best being fully transparent and accountable, and we demand fiscal responsibility. I will continue to work relentlessly to change the status quo, strengthen taxpayer protections, and advocate for significant reforms that restore fairness and accountability in one of King County’s most important public offices.
